stem: A grower corrects a suspected nutrient shortage by raising overall fertilizer concentration, but root-zone EC also rises and symptoms worsen. What should be reconsidered first?
choices: Whether excessive concentration or a root-zone availability imbalance is contributing to the worsening symptoms
Whether the fertilizer concentration should be raised further while holding irrigation frequency constant to test the original deficiency hypothesis
Whether the visual symptom should be matched to a different single-element deficiency chart before considering the measured root-zone EC trend
Whether the nutrient recipe should be changed to a higher-ratio product while keeping total EC similar so the suspected deficient element receives more emphasis
rationale: When higher fertilizer concentration is accompanied by rising root-zone EC and worsening symptoms, excess concentration or impaired root-zone conditions should be reconsidered rather than assuming more fertilizer is required.
